children: InnoCare Pharma said China’s CDE approved its IND for ICP-B161, a bispecific antibody targeting TL1A and IL‑23p19 for autoimmune diseases including IBD. It is the company’s fifth novel drug candidate to enter clinical development in 2026.
Regulatory greenlight moves the asset into human studies, expanding the pipeline and potential future revenue.
Dual mechanism could differentiate in IBD; no approved TL1A/IL‑23p19 bispecifics exist.
Long-acting profile may boost adherence and payer/physician uptake if efficacious.
Early efficacy signals de-risk biology but remain non-clinical; human data needed.
Accelerates R&D cadence, increasing optionality but also burn and execution risk.

This is an early-stage regulatory step expanding InnoCare’s autoimmune pipeline beyond its approved drugs. A clinical readout showing safety and efficacy or fast-track designations would turn this into a larger catalyst.
